live.market: Nasdaq-100 (QQQ 1-minute bars from Yahoo Finance as the live proxy)

backtest.common: Common to all: Nasdaq-100 only (backtest: Dukascopy USATECH CFD 1-minute bars, regular hours 09:30-16:00 ET; live: QQQ 1-minute bars). EUR25 risk per trade (size = 25 / stop distance, capped at 20x the account), stop distance = the rule's stop clipped to 0.25%..0.50% of price (so nothing is tiny and 20x leverage is never needed), target as stated (default 2R = 0.5%..1.0% of price), maximum hold 60 minutes, flat by the 15:59 bar, no new signals after 15:45, one position per strategy at a time. Signals are read on completed bars and filled at the next 1-minute open; stop and target in the same bar counts as the stop.

strategies.name: Larry Williams volatility breakout (0.5 x prior range)
strategies.who: Larry Williams, volatility breakout (Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading, 1999)
strategies.attr: Direct. Multiplier 0.5 is the textbook choice (0.25 and 1.0 are also quoted); fixed before testing.
strategies.rules: Level = today's open +/- 0.5 x yesterday's high-low range. First 1-minute close beyond the level (09:35-15:00) triggers a trade in that direction, 1 a day. Stop distance = 0.25 x yesterday's range (clipped). Target 2R.

strategies.name: Larry Williams Oops! (gap outside prior range, return to prior extreme)
strategies.who: Larry Williams, 'Oops!' pattern
strategies.attr: Direct. Williams exits on the first profitable open; we use stop, 2R target and the 60-minute limit.
strategies.rules: If the day opens below yesterday's low, go long when a 1-minute close is back above that low (opens above yesterday's high: short when back below it), before 13:30, 1 a day. Stop beyond the day's extreme so far (clipped). Target 2R.

strategies.name: Crabel NR7 day + 15-min range breakout
strategies.who: Toby Crabel (NR7 / narrow-range days precede trend days)
strategies.attr: Direct (NR7 pattern). Opening range length (15 min) is our choice.
strategies.rules: Only the day after a narrow-range-7 session (yesterday's range smaller than each of the 6 sessions before it). Long when a 1-minute close is above the first-15-minute high, short below the low (09:45-14:00, 1 a day). Stop distance = the 15-minute range width (clipped). Target 2R.

strategies.name: Zarattini-Barbon-Aziz 5-min ORB (first-candle direction)
strategies.who: Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz, 'A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market' (SSRN 2024); earlier QQQ/TQQQ ORB work by Zarattini & Aziz
strategies.attr: Direct, but the paper's headline result is for 'Stocks in Play', not an index. Their stop is 10% of ATR14 and they hold to the close; ours is clipped to 0.25% and capped at 60 minutes.
strategies.rules: Direction of the first 5-minute candle: bullish -> long only, bearish -> short only (doji = nothing). Enter when a 1-minute close breaks that candle's high (long) or low (short), 09:35-15:00, 1 a day. Raw stop = 10% of the 14-session average daily range (always below the 0.25% floor, so the floor applies). Target 2R.

strategies.name: Mark Fisher ACD (A-point break with pivot-range filter)
strategies.who: Mark B. Fisher, The Logical Trader (ACD method)
strategies.attr: Loose. A-value = 10% of the 10-session average range and a 15-minute opening range are OUR conventions (Fisher uses market-specific values); the C-point and number line are not implemented.
strategies.rules: Opening range = first 15 minutes, A = 0.10 x 10-session average range. Pivot range from yesterday's H/L/C ((H+L+C)/3 +/- ((H+L+C)/3 - (H+L)/2)). Close above range high + A and above the pivot range -> long; below range low - A and below it -> short (until 13:30, 1 a day). Stop = distance to the opening-range midpoint (clipped). Target 2R.

strategies.name: Raschke Holy Grail (ADX>30 trend, pullback to 20-EMA, 5-min)
strategies.who: Linda Raschke, 'Holy Grail' setup (Street Smarts / AIQ interview)
strategies.attr: Direct, run on 5-minute bars as Raschke said it can be.
strategies.rules: ADX(14) above 30 and rising, +DI above -DI, a completed 5-minute bar whose low touches the 20-EMA -> long when a 1-minute close breaks that bar's high within 15 minutes (mirror for shorts). Stop under the pullback bar low, clipped. Target 2R. Up to 4 a day.

strategies.name: Gap fade (gap 0.25-0.5%, target the gap fill)
strategies.who: Gap fill / gap fade - day-trading folklore; NQ small gaps fill most often (perfiltrade.com, tradingstats.net gap studies)
strategies.attr: LOOSE: no single famous author. Same-session fill rates quoted for NQ: 62% for 0.25-0.5% gaps.
strategies.rules: Gap of 0.25%-0.50% (up or down). Fade when a 1-minute close breaks the first-5-minute range against the gap (09:35-11:00). Target = the gap fill (yesterday's close), only if at least 0.25% away; stop = distance to the other end of the 5-minute range (clipped). 1 a day.

strategies.name: Raschke 80-20 reversal
strategies.who: Linda Raschke & Larry Connors, 'Street Smarts' (1995), the 80-20 setup
strategies.attr: Direct, adapted: they use 15-minute bars and ticks, we use 1-minute closes and 0.05%.
strategies.rules: Yesterday opened in the top 20% of its range and closed in the bottom 20% (or the reverse). Today price must first trade 0.05% beyond yesterday's low (high), then a 1-minute close back above (below) that level triggers a long (short) before 15:00. Stop below the new day low (above the new high), clipped. Target 2R.

strategies.name: Gap-and-go (gap >= 0.5%, continue on opening-range break)
strategies.who: 'Gap and go' - day-trading folklore; for NQ, large gaps tend to persist intraday (mpmmarkets.com gap research)
strategies.attr: LOOSE: no single famous author. The 0.5% threshold follows published NQ gap-fill tables (fills drop to 45% above 0.5%).
strategies.rules: Gap = today's open vs yesterday's close of at least 0.5%. Gap up: long when a 1-minute close breaks the first-5-minute high (09:35-11:00); gap down: short on a break of the low. Stop = distance to the opposite end of the 5-minute range (clipped). Target 2R. 1 a day.

strategies.name: Bollinger band reversion to the middle band (15-min, 20/2)
strategies.who: Connors & Alvarez, 'Bollinger Bands Trading Strategies That Work' (2009) / mean reversion to the middle band
strategies.attr: Loose. Their tests are daily; this is a 15-minute adaptation. A published NQ/ES 15-minute band-fade test lost money (cemarketsolutions.com).
strategies.rules: 15-minute bars, Bollinger(20, 2): a close below the lower band -> long, above the upper band -> short, but only if the middle band is at least 0.25% away (no tiny targets). Target = the middle band, stop = same distance clipped to 0.25-0.50%. Up to 4 a day.

strategies.name: Crabel opening-range breakout + stretch
strategies.who: Toby Crabel (Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout, 1990)
strategies.attr: Direct. Crabel's own opening range is 30 seconds; we use 5 minutes.
strategies.rules: Opening range = first 5 minutes. Stretch = average over the last 10 sessions of min(high-open, open-low). Long when a 1-minute close is above range high + stretch, short below range low - stretch (09:35-14:30, first trigger only, 1 trade a day). Stop distance = stretch (the stop sits back at the range edge). Target 2R.

strategies.name: John Bollinger squeeze breakout (Method I, 15-min)
strategies.who: John Bollinger, Bollinger on Bollinger Bands: Method I, the squeeze
strategies.attr: Direct rule (BandWidth at a 125-bar low, then a close outside the band), applied to 15-minute bars; Bollinger's exits (Parabolic) are replaced by our stop/target/60-minute limit.
strategies.rules: 15-minute Bollinger(20,2). BandWidth = (upper-lower)/middle at its lowest in 125 bars = squeeze. Within 5 bars after a squeeze, a close above the upper band -> long, below the lower -> short (3 a day). Stop = distance to the middle band (clipped). Target 2R.

strategies.name: Zarattini-Maroy-Barbon noise-area intraday momentum
strategies.who: Zarattini, Maroy & Barbon (Concretum), 'Beat the Market: An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY)' (SSRN 2024)
strategies.attr: Direct, adapted (their test is SPY, 30-minute checks, hold to the close). An out-of-sample test by others found it much weaker (Swedroe).
strategies.rules: Noise area: for each 5-minute slot, sigma = average over the last 14 sessions of |close_slot/open - 1|. Upper = max(today's open, yesterday's close) x (1+sigma), lower = min(...) x (1-sigma). Checked every 30 minutes (10:00-15:30): close above upper -> long, below lower -> short (2 a day). Trailing exit: a 5-minute close back inside max(upper, VWAP) for longs / min(lower, VWAP) for shorts. Target 2R, 60 minutes.

strategies.name: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou intraday momentum (first 30 min -> last 30 min)
strategies.who: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou, 'Market intraday momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 2018
strategies.attr: Direct academic result (S&P 500 ETF 1993-2013, first half-hour predicts the last). Run here on the Nasdaq-100 with a 0.30% protective stop.
strategies.rules: Return from yesterday's close to the 10:00 close. At 15:30 go in the same direction for the last 29 minutes (exit at the close, or stop 0.30%). No target.

strategies.name: Dalton/Steidlmayer Initial-Balance extension (narrow IB)
strategies.who: J. Peter Steidlmayer / James Dalton (Market Profile, Mind Over Markets): initial balance extension
strategies.attr: Loose: the concept (IB = first hour, narrow IBs extend more often) is Market Profile doctrine, the exact rule is ours.
strategies.rules: Initial balance = first 60 minutes. Only if its width is at or below the 10-session average IB width. First 1-minute close above the IB high -> long, below the IB low -> short (10:30-14:00, 1 a day). Stop = distance to the IB midpoint (clipped). Target 2R.

strategies.name: John Carter TTM Squeeze (5-min)
strategies.who: John Carter, TTM Squeeze (Mastering the Trade)
strategies.attr: Indicator rules as published by StockCharts; the exits and 5-minute bars are ours.
strategies.rules: 5-minute bars: squeeze = Bollinger(20,2) inside Keltner(20, 1.5 x ATR). After at least 6 squeezed bars, the first bar where the squeeze releases opens a trade in the sign of the momentum (linear regression of close vs the mid of the 20-bar channel and SMA). Exit after two consecutive momentum declines, stop 2 x ATR (clipped), target 2R, 60 minutes.

strategies.name: Baltussen et al. rest-of-day momentum -> last 30 min
strategies.who: Baltussen, Da, Soebhag & Zhou, 'Hedging demand and market intraday momentum', JFE 2021
strategies.attr: Direct academic result (rest-of-day return predicts the last half hour, 'gamma' hedging). Our version uses open-to-15:30 return.
strategies.rules: Return from the 09:30 open to the 15:30 price. At 15:30 trade the same direction until the close (stop 0.30%, no target).

strategies.name: Raschke/Connors Turtle Soup (20-bar failed breakout, 5-min)
strategies.who: Linda Raschke & Larry Connors, 'Street Smarts' (1995), Turtle Soup
strategies.attr: Direct idea; the book's own exhibit applies it to 10-minute S&P bars ('a 20-bar high that reverses back'). Our 5-minute 20-bar version is an adaptation of the daily rule.
strategies.rules: On each completed 5-minute bar (09:30+, up to 15:30): the bar makes a new low below the previous 20-bar low (that low at least 4 bars old) but closes back above it -> long (mirror: new 20-bar high that closes back below -> short). Stop beyond the bar's extreme, clipped. Target 2R. Up to 6 a day.

strategies.name: Turtle / Donchian 20-bar breakout (5-min, 10-bar exit)
strategies.who: Richard Dennis / William Eckhardt, the Turtle system (Donchian 20-bar breakout, exit on 10-bar opposite extreme, 2N stop)
strategies.attr: Direct rules, but on 5-minute bars instead of daily bars and without the Turtle position-adding. The 'skip after a winner' rule is not used.
strategies.rules: A 1-minute close above the highest high of the last 20 completed 5-minute bars (or below the lowest low) from 09:40 to 15:00 -> trade that way. Exit when a 5-minute close crosses the 10-bar opposite extreme. Stop 2 x ATR(14) (clipped), target 2R, 15-minute cool-off, up to 4 a day.

strategies.name: Connors RSI(2) mean reversion (5-min, 200-bar trend filter)
strategies.who: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez, RSI(2) (Short Term Trading Strategies That Work, 2009)
strategies.attr: Direct idea, but Connors' version is DAILY (200-day SMA filter, buy RSI(2)<10, exit above the 5-day SMA). This is a 5-minute adaptation and should be read as 'inspired by'.
strategies.rules: 5-minute bars: close above the 200-bar SMA and RSI(2) below 10 -> long (close below SMA and RSI(2) above 90 -> short). Exit when RSI(2) crosses 70 (30 for shorts), stop 0.25% minimum, target 1.5R, or 60 minutes. Up to 8 a day.

strategies.name: Zarattini-Aziz VWAP trend (cross of VWAP)
strategies.who: Zarattini & Aziz, 'VWAP - The Holy Grail for Day Trading Systems' (SSRN 2023)
strategies.attr: Direct. The paper is always in the market (long above VWAP, short below); we take each VWAP cross as an entry and exit on the cross back. An independent rebuild found the edge much smaller and gone after costs (guanalyser.com).
strategies.rules: Session VWAP from (high+low+close)/3 x volume. On each completed 5-minute bar (10:00-15:30) a close that crosses VWAP opens a trade in the new direction (up to 6 a day, 5-minute cool-off). Exit when a 5-minute close crosses back, or stop (distance from VWAP, clipped), target 2R, or 60 minutes.
